- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.4) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > +10% above recent mean), model often overshoots — cap forecast at +5% above prior high.
- If sentiment shows strong positive momentum (e.g., > 0.3 for 3+ days), model underreacts — raise forecast by 2–5% to align with sentiment.
- Model consistently overestimates early in 30-day horizon — apply 3–5% downward bias for first 7–10 days.
- When sentiment turns negative after a peak, model fails to adjust quickly — delay downward correction by 2–3 days, then apply 3–5% drop.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is > 10% above 18-day average, reduce by 2–4% per day until convergence.
- Sentiment reversal (e.g., from +0.3 to -0.4) triggers model lag — add 1–2 day delay to downward adjustment.
